statement: Four marks are made between 20 and 60 on a number line, splitting the part between them into equal pieces. What number is at the mark closest to 60?

choices.misconception: I found the length of each piece, not the number at the mark.
I found the mark closest to 20 instead of the one closest to 60.
I took the halfway point, but with four marks there is no mark exactly in the middle.
I thought 4 marks make 4 equal pieces, so I used pieces of 10.

hints: Draw it: how many pieces do 4 marks make?
Sketch the line with the two ends and the marks between them, and count the gaps. Share the whole distance equally among the gaps, then step back from 60.
4 marks between the ends make 5 equal pieces. The distance from 20 to 60 is 40.

solutions.reliable: Four marks between the ends make 5 equal pieces. The distance is 60 - 20 = 40, so each piece is 8. The marks are at 28, 36, 44 and 52, so the one closest to 60 is 52. Check: 52 + 8 = 60. The transferable idea: n marks between two ends make n + 1 gaps.

whyOnTest: Equal spacing on a number line, with the marks-versus-gaps slip as the main trap.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
